questions.question: Besides reading the manual, what is the best way to learn about transporting hazardous materials?
questions.correctAnswerText: Attend hazardous materials training courses.
questions.explanation: The manual has information to pass the written exam, but not everything needed to do the job safely. Training courses teach you more about handling hazardous materials.

questions.question: What license do you need to transport hazardous materials?

options.text: A CDL with hazardous materials endorsement.
A CDL with a tank endorsement.

questions.correctAnswerText: A CDL with hazardous materials endorsement.
questions.explanation: You must have a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement to drive any vehicle carrying hazardous materials.

questions.question: What does "RQ" stand for?
questions.correctAnswerText: Reportable quantity
questions.explanation: "RQ" stands for reportable quantity. It may be written instead of an "X" on shipping papers when a reportable quantity of hazardous material must be marked.

questions.question: If a hazardous material package is too small for its label, how should you label it?

options.text: Tie it with other hazardous materials and put a labeled sheet of paper on the outside of the bundle.
Attach the label to a tag that is securely fastened to the package.
Mark it with a large orange dot.
Place it in a box with a warning label.

questions.correctAnswerText: Attach the label to a tag that is securely fastened to the package.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped hazard warning labels must be placed on hazardous materials packages. If the label does not fit on the package, it can be attached to a tag that is securely fastened to the package.

questions.question: What could show that a shipment contains hazardous materials?

options.text: The cargo is stored in cylinder tanks.
The cargo is picked up from a supermarket.
The cargo is packaged in cardboard boxes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cargo is stored in cylinder tanks.
questions.explanation: Cylinders and drums are commonly used to hold hazardous materials. Take proper precautions when transporting materials in these containers.

questions.question: What do you need to know to choose the correct placards?

options.text: The hazard classes of the materials.
The types of containers holding the materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: The hazard classes of the materials.
questions.explanation: To choose the correct placards, you need to know the hazard class of the materials, the amount being shipped, and the total weight of all hazardous materials in the vehicle.

questions.question: What letters appear on shipping papers and packages when a reportable quantity is being transported?
questions.correctAnswerText: RQ
questions.explanation: When a substance is transported in a reportable quantity, the shipper must display the letters "RQ" on both the shipping paper and the package.

questions.question: Shippers package hazardous materials in order to ____ them.
questions.correctAnswerText: Contain
questions.explanation: Shippers package hazardous materials to completely contain them. Vehicles should display placards to show what cargo they carry.

questions.question: If your vehicle carrying explosives breaks down, how may you warn other drivers?

options.text: By standing on the roadway and waving your arms.
By keeping the driver's side door open.

questions.correctAnswerText: With electric lights.
questions.explanation: When your vehicle breaks down while carrying explosives, warn other drivers with reflective triangles or electric lights. Do not use flares or other warning signals that could cause the cargo to catch fire.

questions.question: If you find a cargo leak, how should you identify the leaking hazardous materials?
questions.correctAnswerText: Use the shipping papers.
questions.explanation: If you discover a cargo leak, use the shipping papers, label, or package location to identify the materials. Never touch or smell leaking materials because this could cause serious injury or death.

questions.question: Who must mark and label materials for shipping?
questions.correctAnswerText: The shipper
questions.explanation: The shipper must warn drivers and others about hazardous materials. They do this by putting warning labels on packages, placing placards on vehicles, and providing shipping papers and emergency response information.

questions.question: If you discover leaking cargo, you should:

options.text: Touch the leaking material to identify the cargo.
Use shipping papers and labels to identify the leaking cargo.
Assume all the cargo is leaking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use shipping papers and labels to identify the leaking cargo.
questions.explanation: If cargo is leaking, identify it using shipping papers and labels. Do not touch the leaking material.

questions.question: Emergency response information from the shipper must include:

options.text: Any risks of fire or explosion.
How many people should respond in an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any risks of fire or explosion.
questions.explanation: Emergency response information must include material descriptions and names, health hazards, fire or explosion risks, what to do if there is an accident, how to fight fires, how to handle spills or leaks, and first aid steps.

questions.question: Hazardous materials may be transported by:

options.text: Any driver, as long as the total weight is under 50 pounds.
Any driver in a rural area.
A driver with a CDL and HazMat endorsement.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver with a CDL and HazMat endorsement.
questions.explanation: You must have a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement to drive any vehicle that transports hazardous materials.

questions.question: To operate a vehicle that transports hazardous materials, you must have:

options.text: A CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement.
A CDL with a passenger endorsement.
A CDL with an air brake endorsement.

questions.correctAnswerText: A CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement.
questions.explanation: You must have a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement before driving any vehicle used to transport hazardous materials, even if it is not carrying hazardous materials at that time.

questions.question: If hazardous material cargo catches fire, you should:

options.text: Try to put out the fire with a fire extinguisher.
Contact emergency personnel and let them battle the fire.
Continue driving to the fire department.

questions.correctAnswerText: Contact emergency personnel and let them battle the fire.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials fires require special training and equipment. Let emergency personnel handle the fire unless you have this training and equipment.

questions.question: Many poisonous products are also:
questions.correctAnswerText: Flammable.
questions.explanation: Many hazardous materials classified as poisonous are also flammable.

questions.question: Opening trailer doors during a cargo fire may expand the fire because it:

options.text: Changes the temperature of the trailer.
Provides more moisture to the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allows oxygen into the trailer.
questions.explanation: Opening trailer doors during a cargo fire allows oxygen to enter. This can cause the fire to flare up and spread.

questions.question: If a box contains liquid containers, it must display:

options.text: Arrows pointing in the correct upright direction.
The number of containers inside the box.

questions.correctAnswerText: Arrows pointing in the correct upright direction.
questions.explanation: Boxes with liquid containers must have arrows showing the correct upright direction.

questions.question: When refueling a vehicle carrying hazardous materials:

options.text: The engine should be left on.
The engine should be turned off.
The gas nozzle may be left unattended.

questions.correctAnswerText: The engine should be turned off.
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine before refueling a vehicle carrying hazardous materials. Someone must stay at the nozzle and control the fuel flow at all times.

questions.question: Before opening trailer doors during a minor truck fire, what should you do?

options.text: Feel the doors to check if they are hot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Feel the doors to check if they are hot.
questions.explanation: During a truck fire, always feel the doors first to check if they are hot. Hot doors mean there may be a cargo fire inside. If the doors are hot, keep them closed.

questions.question: If "Inhalation Hazard" appears on shipping papers, what placard must the shipper provide?

options.text: Poison Gas or Poison Inhalation Hazard

questions.correctAnswerText: Poison Gas or Poison Inhalation Hazard
questions.explanation: When "Inhalation Hazard" is shown on shipping papers or packages, you must display either a "Poison Inhalation Hazard" placard or a "Poison Gas" placard.

questions.question: Containers of hazardous materials must be:

options.text: Secured to prevent movement during transportation.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secured to prevent movement during transportation.
questions.explanation: Containers of hazardous materials must be secured so they cannot fall, slide, or move around while the vehicle is being transported.

questions.question: A hazardous materials placard is shaped like a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Diamond.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials warning placards are diamond-shaped.

questions.question: Where should a placard be placed?

options.text: At least three inches away from any other markings.
Under a ladder if space is limited.
On a background that is the same color as the placard.

questions.correctAnswerText: At least three inches away from any other markings.
questions.explanation: A placard must be placed at least three inches away from any other markings. Keep it clear of doors, ladders, and other attachments. Always place placards on a background with a contrasting color.

questions.question: A driver should ensure that:

options.text: The shipping paper matches the markings and labels on packages.
The shipping paper is written in code.
All packages are labeled as poison.
The shipping paper is not in the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The shipping paper matches the markings and labels on packages.
questions.explanation: Compare shipping papers to the package markings and labels. Make sure the shipper included the correct description on the shipping paper and that it matches what is on the packages.

questions.question: If Class 3 flammable liquids need to be moved to another tank, they:

options.text: May be transferred on the roadway if no other people are nearby.
Should not be transferred on public roads unless it is an emergency.
Should be kept secret when moved to another tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should not be transferred on public roads unless it is an emergency.
questions.explanation: Flammable liquids should not be transferred from one vehicle to another on public roads, except during emergencies. Always warn others about the hazards of these materials.

questions.question: A sign that your shipment contains hazardous materials is:

options.text: The shipper deals in fireworks or munitions.
Your last shipment was labeled hazardous.

questions.correctAnswerText: The shipper deals in fireworks or munitions.
questions.explanation: One sign that a shipment may contain hazardous materials is the type of business the shipper operates. Examples include paint stores, chemical suppliers, scientific supply companies, pest control businesses, farm supply stores, and fireworks or explosives dealers.

questions.question: Containers of nitric acid should be:

options.text: Stacked no more than two containers high.
Loaded on top of other products.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stacked no more than two containers high.
questions.explanation: Nitric acid containers may be stacked, but only up to two containers high. They should never be stacked on top of other products.

questions.question: ____ identical placards must be placed on a vehicle transporting hazardous materials.
questions.correctAnswerText: Four
questions.explanation: When hazardous materials placards are required, place them on all four sides of the vehicle.
